content:
Hi people! :wave:

A while ago I started to build a small library of theorems and proofs around Existential Rules (aka. Tuple-Generating Dependencies) in Lean.
https://github.com/monsterkrampe/Existential-Rules-in-Lean

Existential Rules and their accompanying reasoning algorithm, called the "chase", are widely studied in Database Theory and Knowledge Representation in CS. Broadly speaking, the chase takes a set of rules and an initial set of facts (called database) and computes further facts to satisfy all the rules in the most general way. This might require infinitely many "chase steps". In the presence of disjunctions, the chase is branching out to produce a set of fact sets to capture all "possible worlds". As of now, the following results have been proven, shamelessly revolving around my own research:

  • The result of the chase is a universal model set. That is, (1) each fact set in the result indeed satisfies all rules and (2) for any given model M of the rule set and the database, we can find a fact set in the chase result that can be homomorphically embedded into M. This is the essential property of the chase.
  • A chase sequence without "alternative matches" on rules without disjunctions yields a universal model that is a core. (Section 3 of this paper)
  • If a rule set is model-faithful acyclic (MFA), then every chase sequence on every database terminates. (The formalization is inspired by Section 3.1 in this paper; MFA was originally introduced here.)
  • A generalization of both Disjunctive MFA (DMFA) and Restricted MFA (RMFA). (For DMFA see Section 3.2 in this paper. For RMFA see Section 4 of this paper.)

On my personal roadmap, the next goal is to prove correctness of some non-termination conditions for the chase (MFC/DMFC/RPC). :road_trip:
There are plenty of other directions to go into of course and I'd be happy to have some collaborations on pushing this topic or also related matters from the fields of Database Theory and Knowledge Representation. I'd also be open to the idea of bringing my project closer to e.g. CSLib, if people think that this makes sense.

If you want to get in touch, just drop me a message! :blush:

Cheers! :tada:
Lukas
